# `non-idiomatic-name`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: official · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: `function-case`

Reports declarations that do not follow Zig's function, type, or variable naming
conventions.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Consistent casing communicates a declaration's role before its type is inspected
and keeps APIs familiar to Zig readers.

## When it fires

It skips exported, extern, escaped, and uncertain declarations where renaming
could affect an external contract, including functions with a non-Zig calling
convention (`callconv(.c)`, `callconv(lib.calling_conv)`), which C callers name,
and declarations the file exports with `@export(&name, ...)`. C-style constants matching
`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` (`O_RDONLY`, `MAX_PATH`) keep the spelling of the API they
mirror, declarations documented as `Deprecated` keep their old name for
existing callers, an underscore may separate digit groups in a type name
(`Sha3_256`), and trailing underscores that tell a name apart from another
(`Details_`, `type_`) do not change its case. A type is recognized from the declaration an unqualified name
resolves to in scope, so a type function in one container does not make an
unrelated value elsewhere look like a type.

Functions that do not return a type use camelCase, as Zig's style guide asks;
set `function-case` to `"snake_case"` for projects that name functions that
way.

`zig-analyzer check` also accepts the casing a project has chosen for a kind
of declaration (functions, types or constants), when at least 20 of them and
90% of the project's use it, as tigerbeetle does snake_case functions: such
names follow the project's convention and are not reported, and a name that
follows neither is reported with both conventions named. A `function-case`
set in `zig-analyzer.json`, in the rule's options or in an override matching
the file, is the project's stated choice and outranks the majority for
functions: only names in the configured case pass.
[`minority-naming-style`](minority-naming-style.md) reports names that depart
from the project's choice. The editor checks one file at a time and sees no
project majority, so set `function-case` there.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn Compute_total() void {}
```

## Options

Set these in the rule's object in `zig-analyzer.json`, next to `level`:

```json
{
  "lints": {
    "rules": {
      "non-idiomatic-name": {
        "level": "warning",
        "function-case": "camelCase"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- `function-case` (default `"camelCase"`): the spelling of functions that do not
  return a type, `"camelCase"` or `"snake_case"`.

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Names>
